assertions.requirement: A listener Job submitted with --host-docker and --require-nested-virtualization on a nested-capable type completes with exit 0, its probe passing every check as the image's non-root user.
docker run, a docker build and a two-service docker compose up with name resolution run through the host's socket, and an inner bind mount of $PWD sees the Job's /workspace.
assertions.candidateEvidence: test/integration/e2e/internal/targets/host-docker-probe.ts: docker_run, docker_build, compose and bind_mount checks.

assertions.requirement: /dev/kvm opens read-write, KVM_GET_API_VERSION is 12 and a real-mode guest runs to its marker and halt.
The host's docker inspect of the Job container shows Privileged false, no added capabilities, no security options and /dev/kvm as its device.

The host daemon has mirror.gcr.io configured as its registry mirror, and a plain Docker Hub name pulls; a plainly published port is reached from a bridge container at host.docker.internal (host-gateway), as a container: job's service, and from a --network host container on localhost, as a workflow's services: ports.

Not probed live: every Azure Job VNet is 10.0.0.0/16, so a peer Job would probe its own address. Isolation from other machines comes from the per-Job VNet and NSG; the host's DOCKER-USER guard is covered by unit tests and a local dind proof.
assertions.candidateEvidence: test/integration/e2e/internal/targets/job-profiles.ts: azure hostDocker.peer false; test/integration/e2e/internal/contracts/dedicated-job.ts: #hostDockerMember submits no prober.

assertions.requirement: Persisted terminal cleanup, complete attempt history and independent native absence are required before release; only one family completion follows.
